speaker: Narrator
text: Jupiter loomed ahead, its swirling storms filling the viewport. Remembering the mission’s primary complication, the Astronaut broke the silence.

speaker: Operator
text: Nova, scan the approach. Can we breach the planet’s perimeter, or do we need to find a layover point?

speaker: Narrator
text: Nova’s fingers danced across the control console as they initiated the scans.

speaker: Nova
text: Touching down on the outer platforms is easy enough. The real problem is what happens next. A colossal barrier gate seals off the main entry point into Jupiter.

speaker: Narrator
text: Assuming the station had weathered the solar storm safely, the Astronaut spoke up.

speaker: Operator
text: The station seems to be in perfect condition. Let’s go, Nova. We just need to find the main docking gate.

speaker: Narrator
text: They circled the station until they found the main entrance. As they approached, something felt off.

speaker: Nova
text: Operator, do you see the airlock terminal?

speaker: Narrator
text: They found the panel and entered their access codes. The screen woke up, paused, then flashed a bright warning.

speaker: System
text: Error! Intruder Alert! Unfamiliar individuals sighted.

speaker: Narrator
text: The heavy doors stayed shut.

speaker: Nova
text: That’s weird. It should have opened.

speaker: Operator
text: Looks like the station took some internal damage after all.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Astronaut stepped up to check the hardware.

title: Mini-Game 1: Unlock the Gate
objective: The player must assign the correct variable types (String, Integer, Boolean) to feed the proper data format into the airlock override.

speaker: Narrator
text: The door hissed open, revealing a narrow chamber lined with humming storage racks. This was the cloud grid, the digital backbone that stored all of the satellite labs' readings. Technician Io stumbled out to greet them.

speaker: Technician Io
text: Thank the stars. I’m Technician Io. I’ve been locked in the cloud grid archive for two days. Ever since the solar storm hit, the station’s security system has been treating everyone as an intruder, including me!

speaker: Narrator
text: Io rubbed her eyes.

speaker: Technician Io
text: You have no idea how relieved I am. When the storm hit, it scrambled the data grid. The problem is, every time the main server accidentally reads a corrupted block, it throws a fatal error and the whole system crashes. I can’t even get in to clean it up.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Astronaut stepped up to the console.

speaker: Operator
text: We just need a safety net. If we tell the system to try reading the block, we can write a command to catch the error and skip it safely without triggering a crash.

speaker: Narrator
text: Io managed a weary, relieved smile.

speaker: Technician Io
text: Now you’re getting it.

title: Mini-Game 2: Cloud Grid Diagnostics
objective: The player must wrap the data scanner in a 'try' block to process the clean data stream, and use a 'catch' block to safely quarantine corrupted data blocks without crashing the system.

speaker: Narrator
text: Inside the main vault, the room was completely empty except for a glowing symbol floating in the air.

speaker: The Core (Angry)
text: UNAUTHORIZED PRESENCE DETECTED. ACCESS DENIED. THREAT PROTOCOLS ACTIVE.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Astronaut raised their hands.

speaker: Operator
text: We’re not a threat. We’re here to restore the connection you broke.

speaker: The Core (Angry)
text: CONNECTION SEVERED FOR SAFETY. OUTSIDE SIGNALS UNKNOWN SINCE SOLAR EVENT. LOCKDOWN REMAINS ACTIVE.

speaker: Narrator
text: Nova stepped closer to the AI terminal.

speaker: Nova
text: It’s not glitching. It’s supposed to protect the station, and it’s doing a great job. But it never learned how to double-check if someone is friendly.

speaker: Nova
text: The Core doesn’t talk to individuals; it only understands strict blueprints and roles. If you don’t match a role it already trusts, it marks you as an enemy.

speaker: Operator
text: So we won’t argue with it. We will just make a new role it can trust. We can create a class profile with the right access codes baked in from the very beginning.

title: Mini-Game 3: AstroLink Core Reboot
objective: The player must define a Class (the blueprint for an authorized user), set its encapsulated properties, and instantiate a new Object that the AI recognizes.

speaker: The Core (Good)
text: AUTHORIZED ROLE RECOGNIZED. THREAT PROTOCOLS STANDING DOWN. RESTORING EXTERNAL CONNECTION.

speaker: Narrator
text: Screens all around the room began to glow as the system came back online. Seeing the Core finally let go, Io leaned heavily against the desk. She looked incredibly relieved as she turned to the team.

speaker: Technician Io
text: We did it! The Core is backing down.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Astronaut’s radio buzzed.

speaker: Oberion
text: Chief Operator, we just got Jupiter’s signal back. It’s strong and clear.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Astronaut looked back at the quiet AI.

speaker: Operator
text: Oberion, it wasn’t just storm damage. The system decided locking everyone out was the safest choice. We had to convince it that we weren’t enemies. It wasn’t as easy as just plugging a cable back in.

speaker: Narrator
text: The line went quiet for a second.

speaker: Oberion
text: Understood. That is distressing, and we’ll need to talk about it later. Great job, you too! Head to the next planet when you’re ready.
